transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-03T15:00:00Z (57 minutes)
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rita Gomez (Catalyst Bio - Head ML), Owen Park (Catalyst - Platform Eng), Zoe Lin (Catalyst - CTO)

Summary:
Quick lab readout for week 3 of the pilot. Focus on latency/throughput numbers vs their incumbent provider, discuss routing/fallback playbook, next steps for dedicated slot sizing and security handoff. Some audio dropouts, auto-transcript may have mis-typed 'Redwood Dedicated' as 'Redwood Dedicate' in places.

Topics Covered:
- Bench numbers: p50/p95 latency, sustained throughput, error rates
- Routing: canary vs weighted routing, fallback to smaller model variants
- Tuning: quantization + batching experiments, KV cache warmup strategies
- Security + ops: VPC peering, KMS, audit logs
- Next steps / action items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, um, today we wanted to run through week three bench results and talk routing handoff, Diego will run the numbers but first just a quick check on attendees —
[00:09] Rita Gomez: yep hi, Rita here, Owen and Zoe are on, thanks Maya. audio's a little low for me but it's okay.
[00:15] Diego Alvarez: cool, i'm diego, i'm the se on this, i'll start with the baseline comparison table — note that some names in the export are a little mangled, like IncumbentAI shows as 'in competitor a i' sometimes, sorry, transcript is messy.
[00:27] Diego Alvarez: ok slide 1, p50 latency: Redwood test harness (single region) p50 is 84 ms, p95 is 210 ms, error rate 0.6%. IncumbentAI reported p50 ~120 ms, p95 ~340 ms, error rate 1.8% on their public endpoints for the same prompt set.
[00:45] Owen Park: where were you running the Redwood tests? which instance type?
[00:49] Diego Alvarez: good question — these runs were on our dedicated pilot pool (GPUTier-A2 equivalent), model quantized to int8 for the speed test, batching disabled for the low-latency path. sequence length median 128 tokens, 95th 480.
[01:05] Rita Gomez: those numbers look promising on p95 but curious about throughput at load — what did you see for sustained qps/throughput?
[01:12] Diego Alvarez: sustained throughput against the workload generator: 320 req/min for the current config under 95% CPU/UTIL; Incumbent on their same hardware baseline showed ~220 req/min before queueing increased p95 by ~30%. we also ran a peak burst test — Redwood handled 4x burst for short windows with graceful degradation; incumbent had timeouts above 2.5x.
[01:36] Zoe Lin: were both systems using prefix caching / kv cache? because warm cache changes the numbers a lot.
[01:40] Diego Alvarez: yes we warmed KV cache for all runs. we saw cache hit rates > 92% for our test set. there's some noise in the incumbent's public logs about cache expiry causing p95 spikes mid-run.
[01:51] Maya Chen: also want to call out unit cost: once quantized and batched optimally, our projected per-1k-token cost is about 0.28 USD vs incumbent at 0.37 USD in their reserved pool. that's rough but directionally important for ROI.
[02:05] Rita Gomez: that delta is attractive, though Zoe will want security assurances before shifting more traffic.
[02:11] Zoe Lin: yeah, security first — i need to see VPC peering diagram, KMS integration details, and audit log retention.
[02:18] Maya Chen: understood, i already flagged the security pack; we'll send SOC2 excerpt and the VPC/KMS quickstart after the call.
[02:24] Owen Park: quick question on routing — you mentioned fallback to smaller model variants, does that change tokenization or output fidelity?
[02:31] Diego Alvarez: small amount of fidelity variance, yes. fallback flow is model-compatible (same tokenizer) but smaller context and fewer parameters, so higher hallucination risk on rare prompts; we recommend A/B test on low-risk traffic before full switch.
[02:45] Rita Gomez: okay, that's fine. next, any oddities in the test logs?
[02:50] Diego Alvarez: we saw an intermittant 502 spike at 00:42 in the run logs, traced to a transient kernel OOM on one node during warmup; we've mitigations: kernel retry, and will pin that node to a higher mem profile for next run.
[03:05] Maya Chen: thanks, diego — can you run the same workload but with batching enabled to see tail latency and throughput tradeoffs?
[03:11] Diego Alvarez: yes — i've scheduled a quantize+batching run for seq_len 512, will attach full trace and flamegraphs.
[03:17] Owen Park: please also include the per-token CPU/GPU time so we can map to our infra costs.
[03:22] Diego Alvarez: will do.
[03:24] [00:03:24] (brief audio dropout)
[03:35] Rita Gomez: on the subject of production readiness, SLA expectations — what's Redwood's SLO for this tier?
[03:40] Maya Chen: for Dedicated pilot pools we guarantee 99.5% uptime for the serving runtime and aim for p95 under 350 ms in normal conditions; we'll include fallback to hosted variants for graceful degradation. if you need higher we can discuss a premium SLA.
[03:55] Zoe Lin: for compliance, we need audit log retention to 1 year and SSO via SAML; also need role-based access.
[04:03] Maya Chen: yes we support SAML SSO and RBAC; audit log retention is configurable — i'll share the exact retention options in the security pack.
[04:12] Owen Park: a practical ops ask — can we get a readonly view to the bench logs? that'd speed triage.
[04:17] Rita Gomez: yes please, we can give a service account.
[04:21] Diego Alvarez: perfect. once we have read-only log access we can reproduce the transient spike and attach the timeline to the run.
[04:30] Maya Chen: ok on routing playbook — short summary: 1) start routed traffic at 10% -> 2) monitor p95 and error rate for 24h -> 3) increase to 50% if stable -> 4) use model fallback for tail events. we also suggest a canary region test for data residency checks.
[04:49] Rita Gomez: how do we configure automatic fallback thresholds? is that in the console?
[04:54] Diego Alvarez: yes, in console under Routing -> Fallbacks, you can set p95 threshold and error thresholds; if exceeded traffic is re-routed to fallback model/region or to the incumbent if you choose. there's also graceful backoff to avoid flip-flopping.
[05:08] Zoe Lin: can the fallback route to our on-prem model? we have an in-house small model for sensitive workloads.
[05:13] Diego Alvarez: currently Redwood can route to private endpoints if you expose them via VPC peering + secure endpoint. we can add it to the routing table. we may need to validate auth and certs.
[05:25] Owen Park: re: dedicated slot sizing, what's the recommended headroom?
[05:29] Diego Alvarez: we recommend 20-30% headroom above 95th percentile load; for your current peak that maps to two medium slots with burst capacity enabled. we'll run a sizing call to confirm.
[05:40] Rita Gomez: i'd prefer we keep one on-call window while we ramp to reduce risk.
[05:44] Maya Chen: agreed, we can include an ops rotation for the pilot phase.
[05:47] Zoe Lin: any surprises in the audit or dependency checks?
[05:50] Diego Alvarez: only the kernel OOM; no suspicious network calls or PII leaks in the logs.
[05:55] Maya Chen: ok last bit — Diego, when you run the quantize+batching test, please also run an A/B on tokenization edge cases — the bot sometimes tokenizes rare unicode oddly and that can change token counts.
[06:09] Diego Alvarez: good call, will add it.
[06:12] Rita Gomez: timeline — we want to decide by end of next week if we move 20% traffic for a 2-week canary. realistic?
[06:18] Maya Chen: yes, with the log access and the extra runs we'll get you the numbers and the playbook; target decision meeting on 2025-10-10.
[06:25] Zoe Lin: fine.
[06:27] Maya Chen: i'll recap next steps and action items after the call. thanks everyone.

- Risk: small delta in output fidelity on fallback models; one transient OOM traced, will be mitigated.
